K-Means Clustering Core Concepts:
Clustering groups observations using selected features. Customer income and spending score, movie year and revenue, or flower petal measurements form feature vectors. A cluster index identifies a group within one fit; relabeling group indices preserves the grouping.

## The objective and update

Choose k centers. Assign each point to its nearest center using Euclidean distance, then replace each center with the coordinate means of its assigned points. Repeat until the largest center movement is within a stated tolerance or the iteration budget is exhausted.

Euclidean distance is sqrt(sum((x_j-y_j)^2)). A centroid averages each coordinate separately. Inertia is the sum of squared distances from every point to its assigned center. The mean minimizes squared distance within that assigned group, which explains the update step.

## Worked update

Use the one-dimensional observations 0, 2, 10 and 12, with initial centers 0 and 10.

| Observation | Distance to 0 | Distance to 10 | Assigned center |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 10 | First |
| 2 | 2 | 8 | First |
| 10 | 10 | 0 | Second |
| 12 | 12 | 2 | Second |

The new centers are (0+2)/2=1 and (10+12)/2=11. Inertia is (0-1)^2+(2-1)^2+(10-11)^2+(12-11)^2=4. Assigning again retains these groups and means, so the next center movement is zero.

Starting both centers at 0 sends tied assignments to the earlier center and leaves the other group empty. An empty group has no mean. The supplied implementation moves a faraway point from a group with more than one member, then computes every group mean. Seeded distinct initial centers reduce this failure but do not replace the repair rule. The iteration cap makes termination finite when the tolerance is not reached.

## Units and scaling

A revenue difference of millions can dominate a year difference of decades. Standardize a numeric column as z=(x-mean)/population_standard_deviation; a constant column uses scale 1. Record the fitted means and scales and reuse them for a later query.

For 0,2,10,12, the mean is 6 and population variance is (36+16+16+36)/4=26. Scaling this one coordinate divides its squared-distance sum by 26: the same partition has standardized inertia 4/26. Raw and standardized inertia use different coordinates.

The source fits standardized features, then inverse-transforms its centers for plots in the original units. Scaling represents a modelling choice about relative feature importance. A descriptive exploration may fit its scaler on the explored observations; a claim about unseen observations needs its preprocessing and evaluation boundary defined before fitting.

## Compare the results

The supplied programs compare two k values across seeds 7, 19 and 31. For each fixed k, compare inertia and membership across seeds. Larger k can lower inertia simply by adding centers, so judge the k comparison using data meaning and a second measure.

Silhouette compares mean distance a to other points in the same group with the smallest mean distance b to another group: s=(b-a)/max(a,b). For point 0 above, a=2 and b=(10+12)/2=11, giving 9/11. Point 2 has b=(8+10)/2=9, giving 7/9. The other points are symmetric; mean silhouette is 79/99. Higher values indicate separation under that distance. The library convention gives a singleton zero; single-group and all-singleton partitions have no defined overall silhouette.

Adjusted Rand agreement compares membership while allowing indices to change. Labels [0,0,1,1] and [8,8,3,3] describe the same partition and have agreement 1. Values near zero indicate chance-level agreement under its adjustment. This compares partitions rather than measuring classification accuracy or proving meaningful categories.

## One fitted library pipeline

This complete small example reuses its fitted scaler when interpreting centers:

    from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
    from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

    points = [[0, 0], [2, 0], [10, 10], [12, 10]]
    pipeline = Pipeline([
        ("scale", StandardScaler()),
        ("cluster", KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10,
                          random_state=7, max_iter=300, tol=1e-6)),
    ])
    pipeline.fit(points)
    model = pipeline.named_steps["cluster"]
    labels = model.labels_
    centers_raw = pipeline.named_steps["scale"].inverse_transform(
        model.cluster_centers_
    )
    print(labels, centers_raw)

Read labels and centers from that fitted model. Calling fit again performs another fit. The supplied manual customer result uses one initialization per seed, while the library comparison uses ten; retain that distinction when interpreting their objectives.

Customer groups describe the supplied observations. Movie groups depend on year, revenue and scaling. Flower species can be compared with groups after fitting while remaining outside the input features.
